title: 15-minute microburst slice choreography — hosted API supply plan
content:
Executive summary:
This sheet describes the operational plan for handling 15-minute microbursts to the Hosted API by rehearsing fine-grained GPU slice choreography across regions and AZs. Goal: keep p95 generation latency within targets during 15-minute peaks while maintaining unit economics. We propose an explicit prewarm/rotation schedule plus an on-demand slice pool to provide an effective headroom multiplier of 1.45–1.7 depending on model mix.

Key outcomes (target numbers, global view):
- Observed 99th 15-min microburst (baseline sample week): 4.2M tokens/sec global.
- Target safety capacity (goal): 4.2M * 1.45 = 6.09M tokens/sec provisioned effective capacity.
- Conservative safety plan (high-risk windows): uplift to 1.7x => 7.14M tokens/sec.
- Operational headroom expressed as prewarm slices: aim for ~30–40% of uplift to be prewarmed steady-state, remainder on-demand cold-start amortized by ultra-fast warmers.

Assumptions and inputs (explicit):
- Model classes and token efficiency used for capacity math:
  * small-chat (6–8B family): ~800 tokens/sec per A100-80 slice (single-model steady-state, cached KV).
  * dense-chat (13–33B family): ~220–420 tokens/sec per A100-80 slice depending on quantization and KV hit rates.
  * heavy-chat (65B+): ~60–140 tokens/sec per A100-80 slice.
- Average tokens per request in peak window = 120 tokens (weighted mix).
- 15-minute bursts account for ~14% of daily token volume but cause majority of P95 latency violations.
- KV cache hit-rate baseline assumed 26% in microbursts; sensitivity range 15–40%.
- Continuous batching reduces per-token GPU cost but increases tail latency; we set batching cap to preserve p95 < 400ms for 1k-token requests.

Allocation overview (region-level snapshot — sample target for a 6.09M tokens/sec plan):
- us-west (primary): target provisioned capacity = 2.1M tokens/sec (35% of global target).
  * Prewarm slices: 220 x A100-80 equivalent slices (mix: 40% small-chat, 45% dense-chat, 15% heavy-chat)
  * On-demand pool: 120 slices (fast-launch vGPU image)
- us-east (failover + demand): 1.65M tokens/sec (27%)
  * Prewarm slices: 160
  * On-demand: 90
- eu-west: 1.45M tokens/sec (24%)
  * Prewarm slices: 140
  * On-demand: 85
- apac (sg/syd): 0.89M tokens/sec (14%)
  * Prewarm slices: 80
  * On-demand: 50
Notes: slice counts use A100-80-equivalent normalization. We assume bin-packing gives ~10% headroom inside each slice for scheduling jitter.

Calculation example (us-west small-chat portion):
- us-west prewarm small-chat slices = 220 * 40% = 88 slices.
- throughput per slice (small-chat) = 800 tokens/sec => small-chat capacity = 88 * 800 = 70.4k tokens/sec.
- Repeat across dense/heavy contributions to sum to regional target.

Prewarm / rotation policy (operational choreography):
- Prewarm window: maintain prewarmed slices for the top 4 hours around predicted daily peak windows (using historical sliding 7-day forecast).
- Rotation cadence: cycle 8% of prewarm slices every 30 minutes to avoid thermal hotspots and spread memory fragmentation across hosts.
- Fast-warm path: keep lightweight warmers (snapshot of model+KV) that can spin a new vGPU slice in ~22–35s (goal) using ultra-fast kernel caches.
- Cold-start fallback: if fast-warm fails, route to compatible smaller model variant (model-variant fallback table in Confluence).

Autoscaling heuristics and signals:
- Primary signals: tokens/sec moving-average (1m / 5m), infra queue length (requests waiting > 50ms), GPU scheduling backlog (> 60s backlog -> immediate on-demand burn).
- Trigger thresholds for on-demand expansion: sustained 3x baseline growth over 60s or token/sec > 90% of provisioned capacity for >30s.
- On-demand spin-up target: ramp to required slice count within 120s for usual bursts; escalate to emergency routing if > 180s.

Cost vs reliability knobs (tradeoffs):
- More prewarm slices => lower risk and lower p95 tail, higher idle cost. We target ~35% prewarm of uplift in normal plan.
- Increase quantization on dense-chat variants when substrate cost pressure > 12% to trade ~2–5% quality for ~1.25–1.6x throughput.
- Prefer KV cache priming for top-10k prompt prefixes to increase hit rate during anticipated microbursts.

Operational runbook (short):
1) Pre-burst check (T-20 mins): validate prewarm counts per region via infra console; ensure fast-warm images healthy (health-check script id: INF-PRW-CHK).
2) T-5 mins: increase scheduler aggressiveness by lowering batching cap for low-latency endpoints that are sensitive to tail latency (config toggle).
3) Burst active: monitor tokens/sec and scheduling backlog; if on-demand spin > 50% of total slices in region, trigger cross-region fallback policy.
4) Post-burst: hold prewarm for 30 more minutes if spotty tail persists; schedule slice drain and memory defrag during low-util hours.

Open questions / uncertainties (action items):
- Need an A/B test to quantify real-world KV cache hit improvement from snapshot priming vs warmers (Owner: Aisha, ENG-INF-1439).
- Validate fast-warm spin-times across provider types (owner: Priya). Current spin target (22–35s) is optimistic on older hardware.
- Define exact quantization thresholds for dense-chat lineage models (research runbook linked in Confluence).

Links and references:
- Design doc: https://redwood-confluence.internal/display/INF/Microburst+Allocator+Design
- Jira epic: ENG-INF-1427 (Microburst allocator and prewarm orchestration)
- Perf PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3892

Appendix: quick sensitivity table (global tokens/sec targets):
- Observed microburst: 4.2M tps
- 1.25x uplift (low buffer): 5.25M tps
- 1.45x uplift (primary plan): 6.09M tps (recommended)
- 1.7x uplift (conservative): 7.14M tps

Short notes-to-self (raw bullets):
- consider assignment of warmers to GPU hosts by NUMA domain to reduce cross-socket traffic
- log exact warm-up durations (metric id: infra.warmer.spin.ms) for 2-week calibration
- surface headroom burn metric in console (headroom.used_pct_15m)

Status: draft-ish operational sheet; ready for infra-review and SRE run-through.
